extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, OPLA/CRU staff, and patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters) handling reexamination and reissue proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on whether and how to merge copending reexamination (inter partes or ex parte) proceedings, reissue applications, and related matters (fees, petitions, prosecution practice, interference coordination) for a single patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement (35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All inter partes reexamination proceedings shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement grounds decisions about merging: if merging would 'unduly delay' the first proceeding (i.e., withdraw it from its place in the process and cause delay), the proceedings generally will not be merged. The Office may nevertheless merge if merger would foster special dispatch; decisions are case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: When not to merge due to undue delay
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second request for reexamination will unduly delay the first reexamination proceeding, the two proceedings generally will not be merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid merger when it would delay prosecution of the earlier proceeding; non-merger allows the first proceeding to conclude and the second to be resolved based on claims as indicated in the issued reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain identical amendments in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments in the merged reexamination files (or reissue and reexamination files) for the duration of the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present at the time of merger, the patent owner must submit a 'housekeeping' amendment placing the same amendments in all proceedings. The housekeeping amendment must not address any issue of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping amendment must not address patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: A housekeeping amendment required to make claims identical must not address any issue of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housekeeping amendments are limited to making claim texts identical across files; substantive patentability arguments or amendments are improper in the housekeeping filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for non-identical claims (35 U.S.C. 112, para. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all of the merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 2, as indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit identical claim text across merged files can lead to indefiniteness rejections for lack of particular pointing out of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single combined examiner action and file markings
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is appropriate in merged proceedings, a single combined examiner's action will be prepared containing the control numbers of the two (or more) proceedings on every page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single action cover form (with both control numbers) is used; clerical staff copy and print appropriate data for each request; each requester and the patent owner receive copies; where NIRC is appropriate, plural notices printed and both files processed. CRU prepares concurrent files as specified in MPEP § 2687.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing when decision on Request 1 not yet made
rubrics_metrics.description: If the decision on the reexamination request has not yet been made in Request 1 and Request 1 is grantable, it should be processed to the point where an order granting reexamination is mailed; an Office action should not be mailed with the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request 1 is normally held until Request 2 is ready for the prosecution stage following an order granting reexamination, or until Request 2 is denied. Request 2 should be determined on its own merits without reference to Request 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee, only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one fee need be paid for the patent owner's appellant brief even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No petition to merge necessary; Office will usually act sua sponte
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge multiple reexamination proceedings is necessary since the Office will generally, sua sponte, decide whether to merge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition to merge is filed prior to the order to reexamine the second request it will not be considered and will be returned by OPLA; the return decision will be of record but no copy retained. See MPEP § 2667.

rubrics_metrics.name: When petitions to merge are considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner or a requester may petition to merge at any time after the order to reexamine the second request; petitions by parties other than the patent owner or a third party requester will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of a petition to merge after the order to reexamine the second request is permitted (a waiver of 37 CFR 1.939) to assure merger at the earliest possible stage. Decisions on merits where at least one proceeding is inter partes are made by OPLA; where none are inter partes, decisions are made by the CRU Director or CRU SPE if delegated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of merger guidance to >2 requests and ex parte inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for merger should be extended to situations with more than two requests and to situations where one request is for ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ex parte reexamination is to be included in the merger, allowance must be made for the statement and reply periods provided for in ex parte reexamination after the order granting reexamination is issued. If all proceedings to be merged are ex parte, see MPEP § 2283 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature petitions returned (petitions to stay reexamination because of interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay an inter partes reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the first Office action in the reexamination proceeding will not be considered and will be returned as premature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to stay filed after the first Office action may be filed by the patent owner (and by a party who is both in the interference and a requester) and will be referred to OPLA for decision. Improper petitions (filed by parties not authorized) will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: General policy on reexamination and interference (no automatic stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed or stayed because of an interference or the possibility of an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rationale is the 'special dispatch' requirement; Office will generally proceed simultaneously with necessary decisions in the reexamination and the interference to the extent desirable. The Board has flexibility under 37 CFR 41.103 to tailor solutions when both are copending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements to the Board (37 CFR 41.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at the initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify its real party-in-interest and each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect, or be affected by, the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal and include a copy of the complaint or notice of appeal. See also §§ 1.301–1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction and completion of examination (37 CFR 41.102–41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating a contested case, examination or reexamination must be completed, and there must be at least one claim that is patentable but for a judgment and would be involved in the contested case; the Board acquires jurisdiction when it initiates a contested case and other Office proceedings are suspended except as ordered by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects timing and coordination when reexaminations and interferences/contested cases are copending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert Board to reexamination rejections corresponding to interference counts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner in reexamination rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in an interference, the attention of the Board shall be called to the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the interference takes into account reexamination developments affecting the same claim/count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to suspend interference under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) is disfavored
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination may be made at any time during the interference by any party, but suspension is not favored and normally will not be permitted until an order granting reexamination is issued and motions in the interference have been disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If APJ denies the motion, a request to stay may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.993; such requests are decided by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board notification upon issuance/publication of reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified; the patent owner must notify the Board upon issuance/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification ensures interference proceedings reflect current claim status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of reissue application and inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination proceeding on which an order pursuant to § 1.931 has been mailed are pending concurrently, a decision may be made to merge them or to suspend one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where merged, the merged proceeding will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171–1.179, patent owner required to place and maintain same claims in both, third party requester participation preserved to extent allowed for inter partes, examiner actions apply to both files, and any inter partes reexamination merged with a reissue application shall be concluded by grant of the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification responsibilities when reissue and reexamination copend
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner (reissue applicant) has responsibility to notify the Office when a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding are pending concurrently; file Notifications of Concurrent Proceedings in the appropriate files as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 37 CFR 1.178(b) in the reissue application and 37 CFR 1.565(a) or 1.985 in the reexamination proceeding (depending on ex parte vs inter partes) to notify the Office; hand deliver paper files to OPLA when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for decision on merging or staying reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the examination of a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of the two, will not be made prior to the mailing of the order to reexamine the patent pursuant to 37 CFR 1.931.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on a request must still meet 35 U.S.C. 312(a) timing (within 3 months of the request filing). If reexamination is ordered, the signed order should be promptly forwarded to CRU support for mailing; no first Office action accompanies the decision ordering reexamination. OPLA is notified when proceedings are ready for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for merging reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions to merge or stay are case-by-case and within the sole discretion of the Office to facilitate orderly operation; the status of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding will be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue raises issues not proper for reexamination or comment by a third-party requester, merger ordinarily will not be ordered and one proceeding stayed. Good cause to stay the reexamination may justify Director action under 35 U.S.C. 314(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when reissue issues before or after reexamination decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent will issue before the determination on reexamination must be made, determination should normally be made after granting the reissue patent and based on the reissue patent claims; if reissue issues after reexamination is ordered, subsequent proceedings in the reexamination will be based on the reissue patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue claims must be presented as a 'clean copy' in the reexamination proceeding (no bracketed/italic markup); Form paragraph 22.05 may be used in Office action to note proceedings are based on reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened response periods after removal of stay for merger
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination proceeding has been stayed and the stay is removed following reissue application examination, the first Office action will set a shortened statutory period for response of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer); the second Office action will normally be final and also set one month or thirty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These shortened periods are necessary to prevent undue delay and to proceed with special dispatch in view of the earlier stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application will be examined in the same manner as a non-reissue, non-provisional application and will be subject to applicable rules; reissue applications will be acted on in advance of other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reissue and reexamination are merged, examiner assignment and conduct follow MPEP § 2636 and the merger decision sets the practice and procedure; examiner consults with OPLA RLA before issuing Office actions in merged proceedings.
